before: Chu Pou shrank from wielding power at court, and Wang Shu begged to be sent to the frontier; both kept their skins and their honor, and deserve mention.
after: Chu Pou feared and avoided the power of the court, and Wang Yun insisted on seeking a command away from court; this enabled them to preserve themselves and avoid harm, and their conduct deserves praise.
sourceBasedReason: s0230 explicitly gives 王蘊，字叔仁. 王叔仁 is Wang Yun, not Wang Shu 述. 畏避朝權 means fearing and avoiding court power, not reluctance to wield it; 出鎮 does not specify a frontier, and 全身遠害 does not add preservation of honor.
sourceQuote: 若褚季野之畏避朝權，王叔仁之固求出鎮，用能全身遠害，有可稱焉。
pairedFieldChecked: As for Chu Yeye’s fearing and avoiding court power, and Wang Shuren’s firmly seeking to go out and hold a command, by this they were able to preserve the body and keep far from harm—there is something to praise in that.

before: As for Chu Yeye’s fearing and avoiding court power, and Wang Shuren’s firmly seeking to go out and hold a command, by this they were able to preserve the body and keep far from harm—there is something to praise in that.
after: As for Chu Jiye’s fearing and avoiding court power, and Wang Shuren’s firmly seeking to go out and hold a command, by this they were able to preserve the body and keep far from harm—there is something to praise in that.
sourceBasedReason: 季野 is Jiye, the courtesy name of Chu Pou. The source does not say Yeye. Preserve Wang Shuren as the correctly romanized courtesy-name reference.
sourceQuote: 若褚季野之畏避朝權，王叔仁之固求出鎮，用能全身遠害，有可稱焉。
pairedFieldChecked: Chu Pou shrank from wielding power at court, and Wang Shu begged to be sent to the frontier; both kept their skins and their honor, and deserve mention.

before: Wang Xia, styled Huanzi, was the father of Empress Jianshun, paternal uncle’s son to Grand General Who Gallops as if Flying Shu.
after: Wang Xia, styled Huanzi, was the father of Empress Jianshun and a collateral paternal uncle of Shu, Grand General Who Gallops as if Flying.
sourceBasedReason: 述之從叔 identifies Wang Xia as a collateral paternal uncle of Wang Shu, matching the paired idiomatic. The old literal paternal uncle’s son reverses the generation into a cousin.
sourceQuote: 王遐，字桓子，簡順皇后父，驃騎將軍述之從叔也。
pairedFieldChecked: Wang Xia, courtesy name Huanzi, father of Empress Jianshun, was a collateral paternal uncle of Wang Shu, Grand General Who Gallops as if Flying.
